## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Nikkhepavāra* (Paṭṭhāna 1.1) is the opening section of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh and final treatise of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It provides the initial statement and analytical exposition of the conditional relations; Buddhaghosa's *Visuddhimagga* refers to this exposition of the schedule as the *mātikā-nikkhepa*, citing its treatments of proximity condition (*anantara-paccaya*) and decisive-support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*) [Ñāṇamoli 2010]. English translations of the text have been produced by Nārada Thera and Ayya Agganyani [SuttaCentral].
Textual reuse analysis by DharmaNexus records 9,349 matching passages between the *Nikkhepavāra* and 156 other Pali texts, reflecting the programmatic recurrence of conditional formulas throughout the collection [DharmaNexus]. Its closest internal alignments are with subsequent divisions of the *Paṭṭhāna*, including the *Kusalattika* (Patthana 1.2, 5.1, 7.1, 19.1), *Hetugocchaka* (Patthana 2.1), *Mahantaraduka* (Patthana 2.10), *Upādānagocchaka* (Patthana 2.11), *Piṭṭhiduka* (Patthana 2.13), *Vitakkattika* (Patthana 1.7), and *Vedanāttika* (Patthana 1.3), as well as reference compilations such as the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi* [DharmaNexus]. Substantial textual parallels also appear in commentary and later treatises, including the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Visuddhimagga*, and the *Saṅgāyana-puccha vissajjanā* [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages with cross-tradition philosophical literature, identifying matches in the Tibetan translation of the *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* (D4090), Harivarman's *Satyasiddhiśāstra*, the *Prajñāpradīpaṭīkā* (D3859), and the *Āryākṣayamatinirdeśaṭīkā* (D3994) [DharmaNexus].
